newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - BRITISH BUSINESS - JUNE 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - BRITISH BUSINESS - JUNE 18.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- BUDGET DEFICIT HITS SHARE PRICES

Shares on the London stock exchange fell sharply on Tuesday following the publication of worse-than-expected public finance figures. Investors braced themselves for a tough budget in July after the figures showed that the budget deficit widened to 3.96 billion stg in May, 1 billion stg higher than anticipated. Chancellor Gordon Brown may now use the size of the deficit to justify an increase in taxes.
-- BSKYB CHIEF TO GO ON HEALTH ADVICE

Sam Chisholm is to step down as chief executive of satellite broadcaster BSkyB at the end of the year on the grounds of ill-health. Chisholm, a chronic asthma sufferer, denied industry speculation that his decision has been influenced by a deterioration in relations with Sky owner Rupert Murdoch, or by any disagreement with Murdoch's daughter Elisabeth, head of programming at Sky. Chisholm will be replaced by Mark Booth, currently head of Murdoch's Japanese TV venture JSkyB.
-- RECOVERY TO 6.7 MILLION STG DAWNS AT ALLDAYS

The owners of the Alldays chain of convenience stores and food service company has reported a 24 percent increase in interim pre-tax profits before exceptional gains, to 6.7 million stg. Watson and Philip, which issued a profits warning last October, said it remains on track to exceed 700 owned and franchised Alldays stores this year, and has plans for new initiatives such as Dunkin Donuts and Movie Nights video rentals at the chain.
THE TIMES
-- GRANDMET STAKE FOR LVMH

French luxury goods group LVMH, which is seeking to block the planned merger between drinks giants Guinness and Grand Metropolitan, has acquired a quarter percent stake in GrandMet for 27 million stg. LVMH already owns 14.2 per cent of Guinness, and is expected to use its new stake to present a case for a merger of the spirits businesses of all three companies to other shareholders.
-- ELECTRICITY WATCHDOG ACCUSED OVER LEVY

Offer, the electricity watchdog, has been criticised for failing to ensure that industrial customers get lower prices. The attack follows a survey of electricity prices by National Utility Services, which found that despite lower prices being made possible by the cut in the levy that had largely supported the nuclear industry, not all companies had passed on the savings.
-- ADMINISTRATORS PUT FACIA SHOE BRANDS ON SALE

The administrators for the shoe retailing businesses of the collapsed Facia empire have put the brands up for sale. Price Waterhouse have written to interested parties offering for sale the brand names of Curtess, Freeman Hardy Willis, Manfield, One-Step, Trueform and Trueform Kool Kids.
THE GUARDIAN
-- THAMES IN HOT WATER AGAIN

Privatised water company Thames Water has landed itself in controversy with a warning of looming water shortages and the possibility of restrictions on water use this summer. The announcement came on the day the company reported a 62 percent increase in pre-tax profits to 371.8 million stg, on turnover of 1.28 billion stg. Thames also increased its dividends to shareholders by 22 per cent, at the same time as warning that the government's proposed windfall tax could damage investment.
-- TAKEOVER PANEL FORCES MIRROR TO REVEAL ALL

The takeover panel has forced Mirror Group Newspapers to confirm it is discussing a 250 million stg takeover of Midland Independent Newspapers, a regional press and exhibitions group. The announcement was prompted by a large increase in the price of shares in Midland this week, and it now leaves merchant bank Hambros with the prospect of raising up to 300 million stg to help MGN out of what one analyst dubbed 'a strategic hole 20 years deep'.
-- MOTOROLA ZOOMS INTO SATELLITE VIDEO

Motorola, the US manufacturer of semiconductor chips and telecommunications equipment, has announced plans for a $12.9 billion satellite system. The proposed Celestri system would be a direct challenge to the Teledesic project backed by Boeing and Bill Gates, chairman of Microsoft. Both systems would provide high-speed data and video to international businesses.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- BRITISH GAS FACES PRICE CURBS

The government will publish on Wednesday the long-awaited Monopolies and Mergers Commission report on the charges that British Gas's TransCo pipeline division is allowed to levy. British Gas is bracing for a tough price clampdown, and met with unions Tuesday night to brief them on the outcome. The MMC inquiry was launched after British Gas rejected proposed price cuts from regulator Ofgas that would have been worth 28 pounds stg for domestic customers.
-- BAT CLOSE TO SETTLING LAWSUITS

The US tobacco industry looks set to conclude a landmark deal to resolve hundreds of lawsuits filed by smokers and state governments claiming healthcare costs. The tobacco companies, including BAT, could have faced claims totalling $300 billion. The Washington Post has reported that sources close to talks between the industry and the claimants say that most of the major issues have been resolved, and that agreement could be announced this week.
-- PHILIPS AND LUCENT MERGE

Dutch electronics giant Philips is to merge its telecommunications consumer products division with that of Lucent Technologies of the US. The new company, to be called Philips Consumer Communications, will have annual sales of $2.5 billion and will develop and sell cellular telephones, pagers and related communications products.
